mild.name: Mild pack
mild.description: Shorter horizons, softer decline, looser cushions — often too soft for high-WR plans.

central.name: Central pack (§18 hypotheses)

strict.name: Strict pack

fixtures.name: Plan A — Conservative retiree
fixtures.notes: Modest lifestyle, strong dependable income, large savings, low WR. Should usually hold up.

fixtures.name: Plan B — Average / typical Journey retiree
fixtures.notes: Near ~4% withdrawal rate. Expect holds or sensitive with useful nuance.

fixtures.name: Plan C — Aggressive saver
fixtures.notes: High savings vs gap (~2.5% WR). Should feel reassuring, not “guaranteed.”

fixtures.name: Plan D — High withdrawal rate
fixtures.notes: Large savings gap vs balance (~8%+ WR). Should look vulnerable.

fixtures.name: Plan E — Low withdrawal rate
fixtures.notes: Dependable income covers most spending. Barely moves under stress.

fixtures.name: Plan F — Very long retirement emphasis
fixtures.notes: Moderate ~3.4% WR where longevity extension should matter.

planBCentralDiagnosis.aggregationRuleFired: Two or more severe → Needs. weakerGrowth=severe and earlyDecline=severe. Phase 3 difficult boost did NOT fire (phase3=workable).
planBCentralDiagnosis.whatMakesWeakSevere: weakPath ending balance is 0 (depletes) while basePath lasts full 30y with ending ~$312k → severe via “depletes when base does not”.
planBCentralDiagnosis.whatMakesEarlySevere: earlyPath depletes (year 28) while base does not → severe via same rule. First-year shortfall does NOT fire (after -20% balance is $840k > $42k W).
planBCentralDiagnosis.lateDepletionNote: Early-decline depletion at year 28 of 30 is inside the final 20% of the horizon, but classifyImpact returns severe earlier because “depletes when base does not” takes precedence over the late-depletion noticeable rule.
